newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Southeast power mostly steady in light trade.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Southeast power mostly steady in light trade.

text.p: Spot bulk electricity prices in the U.S. Southeast were mostly steady Friday in sparse trade despite expectations for above-normal temperatures in the region this weekend.
"There's just hardly anyone in the market today. Very few deals have been done," one trader said, noting the holidays and drop in industrial demand were keeping traders absent from the market.
Forecasters said cooler air may arrive early next week, which may trigger additional buying.
Firm, peak power prices in the northern part of the Tennessee Valley Authority (TVA) territory for Monday were still assessed in the $11.00-$13.00 per megawatt hour (MWh) range.
Firm, off-peak electricity in northern TVA was notionally assessed in the $8.50-9.00 range, but no deals could be confirmed done.
At the Georgia/Florida border, prices for firm, peak electricity in 16 hour blocks for Monday delivery were talked higher in the $19.00-20.00 range, as compared with Thursday's $17.00-18.00 range.
Firm, off-peak power for Monday at the Ga./Fla. border was steady at $9.00.

Temperatures in the Southeast are expected to average about four to 12 degrees above-normal through the weekend. Slightly cooler air is expected to arrive early next week, but temperatures are forecast to return to near-normal levels later in the week.
